messages.subject: fatal error: 'string.h' file not found #include_next <string.h>
parts:
Hello Nimble Users,

I am new to Nimble and I am trying to run the NimbleMCMC function in R but I receive a bunc of errors which are:

Error: Failed to create the shared library. Run 'printErrors()' to see the compilation errors.
> printErrors()
In file included from dynamicRegistrations_02_15_14_40_13.cpp:1:
In file included from /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.1/Resources/library/nimble/include/nimble/dynamicRegistrations.h:27:
In file included from /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.1/Resources/library/nimble/include/nimble/RcppUtils.h:26:
In file included from /usr/local/clang4/bin/../include/c++/v1/string:470:
In file included from /usr/local/clang4/bin/../include/c++/v1/string_view:171:
In file included from /usr/local/clang4/bin/../include/c++/v1/__string:56:
In file included from /usr/local/clang4/bin/../include/c++/v1/algorithm:638:
In file included from /usr/local/clang4/bin/../include/c++/v1/cstring:61:
/usr/local/clang4/bin/../include/c++/v1/string.h:61:15: fatal error: 'string.h' file not found
#include_next <string.h>
              ^~~~~~~~~~
1 warning and 1 error generated.
make: *** [dynamicRegistrations_02_15_14_40_13.o] Error 1

I have seen other responses but they were not useful for me. Does anyone has a suggestion please?

Thank you!

Yayo

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: fatal error: 'string.h' file not found #include_next <string.h>
parts:
Dear Yayo,
Thanks for posting the question.
Unfortunately it is really difficult to diagnose a problem like this. 
It appears that something is not standard or not working in your C++ compiler setup.  One way to check, outside of nimble would be to try a simple Rcpp invocation:

Rcpp::cppFunction(
          'int fibonacci(const int x) {
              if (x == 0) return(0);
              if (x == 1) return(1);
              return (fibonacci(x - 1)) + fibonacci(x - 2);
          }')

fibonacci(7)

(nimble does not use Rcpp, but the necessary compiler tools should be the same.). If that doesn't work, the problem you see when using is not from nimble itself.

You listed your Rstudio version but not your R version.  The Rstudio version looks like it is not the latest, so might that also the case for your R version? In the error output, the paths suggest that you are on a 4.1.x version, which is not up to date.  If so, updating both of those would be my first guess at a solution.

Sometimes when people have inscrutable configuration problems, they have had success by starting from scratch: install Xcode (with command-line tools), install R, install nimble.  On rare occasions we've seen a systematic problem from something like a particular OS version, but I'm not aware of that going on at the moment.

HTH
Perry
